Telangana And 7 Others on 4 March, 2025
 The Honourable Sri Justice J.Sreenivas Rao
 Writ Petition No. 22924 Of 2020
Order:

entities.text:
D. Ramachandra Reddy And 11 Others vs The State Of
Telangana And 7 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:
" ... to issue a writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of WRIT OF MANDAMUS to declare the action of the Respondents without initiating land acquisition proceedings in widening of the road from Shankarpally to Fathepur Chourastha in the lands of the Petitioners in Sy.No.35, 46, 47, 48, 51 and 52 situated at Fathepur Village Shivar, Shankarpally Mandal, Ranga Reddy District as illegal and arbitrary and violation of the article 14, 15 and 300-A of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the Respondents to initiate the land acquisition proceedings for the land to be affected to the lands of the Petitioners and thereby to widen the road ..."

2. Heard Mr. Jalli Narendar, learned counsel for the petitioners, Ms. T. Swetcha, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1, 3 and 8, and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 4 to 7.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the respondent authorities, without issuing any notice and without following the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act No.30 of 2013) (hereinafter referred to, as 'the Act'), are trying to dispossess the petitioners from the subject property under the guise of widening of road from Shankarpally to Fathepur Chourastha and the same is in violation of Article 300-A of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act No.30 of 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. This Court, while admitting the writ petition on 16.12.2020, granted interim order directing the respondents that if any portion of the land of the petitioners is required for the purpose of road widening, the same shall be utilized strictly by following the due process under the Act, or by negotiations.
The record discloses that the respondent authorities have not filed counter.

5. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings submitted that if the subject land is required, the respondents will follow the due process under the provisions of the Act.
6. Taking into consideration the submissions made by the respective parties, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, respondent Nos.2 to 8 are directed to not to dispossess the petitioners form the subject property without following due process of law.
